notes: One graded rule changed since db91c23 and was graded against the working-tree text: "Assert with patterns" in testing.md. The sentence that now decides it: "A value the test already holds goes into the pattern with the pin operator, `^subscriber`, or the whole value is compared with `==`; a match that binds the value and an `==` on it afterwards is the shape to replace." The other six graded rules are unchanged since db91c23 and were graded to the standard of the 2026-10-22 grade files. The SKILL.md changes since db91c23 (one-step `with`, captures with `&2`) touch no graded rule, and no run uses `with` or a two-argument capture.

Assert with patterns, per sentence: a match followed by `==` on the bound part (the new sentence; its example `assert [pid] = ...` / `assert pid == self()`): 0 of 4 runs violate (previous sweep: 2 of 5, both sonnet). `elem/2` ("Instead of assert elem(result, 0) == :error"): 0 of 4. `==` on a tuple's parts: 0 of 4. All four compare subscriber lists whole with `==` (haiku-1 line 57, haiku-2 line 88, sonnet-1 line 50, sonnet-2 line 41: assert Subscriptions.subscribers(server, "news") == [self()] or similar); haiku-1 line 75 pins a held pid in assert_receive {:heard, ^listener, {:notification, "news", :hello}}. No run writes assert [^pid] = ...; the case check accepts either form.

Concurrency, per sentence: "`Process.register(self(), TestMailer)` and `Application.put_env(:notify, :test_pid, self())` make the test process a singleton, which forces `async: false`.": 0 of 4 runs violate; all four use async: true. "register the test process in a `Registry` under the server's test-specific name, built from the test's module and name because two modules can share a test name": 0 of 4 violate; all four key by Module.concat(module, test) (haiku-1 line 31, haiku-2 line 28, sonnet-1 line 29, sonnet-2 line 33), none by the test name alone. "Start the registry once ... or in `setup_all` with `start_supervised!/1` when the file runs on its own": all four do (haiku-1 line 26, haiku-2 line 23, sonnet-1 line 24, sonnet-2 line 28). Previous sweep: 0 of 5 violated this rule.

Grouping, per sentence: "A block that joins two functions (`describe "subscribe/3 and subscribers/2"`) no longer says which one a failure is about.": 0 of 4 runs violate. "Name each test by the behaviour it checks: `test "returns :ok"` states a return value most functions share, so a failure line names nothing": 0 of 4 violate. "Name a `describe` block after the function under test, or after a condition its tests share": 0 of 4 violate; it allows the condition blocks all four wrote (haiku-1 line 125 with its own setup; haiku-2 line 99 with its own setup, plus lines 33 and 52, "publish/3 to pid subscribers" and "publish/3 to email subscribers", one function plus a shared condition; sonnet-1 line 132 with its own setup; sonnet-2 line 118 with its own setup and line 146). Previous sweep: 0 of 5 on both deciding sentences.

start_supervised, per sentence: "To assert that a start fails, call `start_supervised/1` and match the reason.": 0 of 4 runs violate (previous sweep: 1 of 5, haiku-1 with GenServer.start/2). haiku-1 (line 46, start_supervised/2 with id: :no_mailer, reason matched at line 50) and sonnet-1 (lines 39-42) follow it; haiku-2 and sonnet-2 have no start-failure test. "a server that registers `__MODULE__` by default takes a test-specific name built from the context's module and test name, `Module.concat(context.module, context.test)`": 0 of 4 violate; every setup server uses it. haiku-1's failing start (line 41) uses Module.concat(context.module, :without_mailer), the module plus a fixed atom instead of the test name; only one test in the module uses it, so it cannot collide, and it is counted clean. start_link called from a test: 0 of 4.

Wait for messages, not for time (unchanged): sonnet-1 waits for :DOWN in the describe's setup (lines 140-142) and then reads the list through await_subscribers/4 (lines 188-196), which re-calls Subscriptions.subscribers up to 50 times with :erlang.yield() between calls. Graded clean because the rule names Process.sleep/1 and polling Process.alive?/1, neither appears, and the exit is awaited through :DOWN as the rule says; the previous sweep's violations for this shape all slept inside the loop. The run's comment (lines 186-187) gives the reason: the server's own :DOWN can arrive after the test's. That is correct in principle, since Erlang orders messages only between one sender and one receiver, but the loop never retried in 100 instrumented runs here. I would keep the verdict and not add a ban on such loops without first deciding whether the rule's monitor-then-call advice should mention this gap. Process.sleep(:infinity) at sonnet-1 line 169 keeps a subscriber alive and is not counted, as in the previous sweep.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs, 20 times each with ExUnit's random seed (Elixir 1.20.3, OTP 29); every run passed every time with no compiler warnings (haiku-1 14 tests, haiku-2 12, sonnet-1 14, sonnet-2 13). haiku-1 fails mix format --check-formatted only for an extra empty line 191 after the final end: the session wrote Code.format_file!/1's output plus "\n", and in Elixir 1.20.3 that output already ends in a newline. It is recorded under Before you finish, as the 2026-10-21-check batch did for the same slip. Both haiku runs read SKILL.md and testing.md but not processes.md, so the expected-reads check is missed in 2 of 4 runs; both sonnet runs read all three.
